summary: Gianpaolo Vetturini is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of London, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Tadeusz Skorupski.

Giei Honda (1888–1953) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Kyoto University (~1910–1914). He served at Kyoto University (lecturer in 1929; adjoint professor 1934–1948), and was a professor at Rissho University and Aichi Bunkyo Women's College.
Giho Okada (1882–1961) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University under Kaiten Nukariya. He later served as a professor at Komazawa University.

Gikyo Ito (1909–1996) specialized in Iranian, Central Asian, and linguistic studies. He studied at Kyoto University under Atsuuji Ashikaga, earning a doctorate in 1953, and taught at Kyoto University, Osaka University of Foreign Studies, Kyoto Sangyo University, and Tokai University.

Gil Fronsdal (born 1954) is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. He completed his PhD at Stanford University (~1989–1998) under Carl Bielefeldt and Bernard Faure, and held positions at the Insight Meditation Center (~1995) and Sati Center for Buddhist Studies (~1997).
Gilbert Kenneth Jenkins (1918–2005) was an Indology, history, and archaeology scholar. He was educated at Bloxham School (~1932–1937) and served on the staff of the British Museum from 1947 to 1978.

Gilles Tarabout studied under Madeleine Biardeau and works in Indology and religious studies. In 2004, he was attested as a senior fellow at CNRS, a member at EHESS, and an exchange program director at the Fondation Maison des Sciences de l'Homme.
Gin Ling Liu is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Hong Kong under the supervision of Jing Yin, also studying under traditional teacher Hsing Yun (all attested 2008).

Giovanni Gentile (1875–1944) was an Italian philosopher who studied at the Scuola Normale Superiore di Pisa and University of Pisa. He held professorships at the Universities of Palermo, Pisa, and Rome, and was president of the Italian Institute for the Middle and Far East.

Giovanni Vacca (1872–1953) was a scholar of sinology and history/archaeology. After studying at the universities of Genoa and Florence, he lectured in Chinese at Florence and held appointments at the University of Rome, including the chair for History and Geography of East Asia.

Giovanni Verardi (born 1947) works in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at the universities of Allahabad, Banaras Hindu, and Gorakhpur, holding posts at Ca' Foscari University, University of Bologna, and University of Naples "L'Orientale" (1988–1993).

Girindrasekhar Bose (1887–1953) was an Indian philosopher and psychologist who studied at Presidency University, Medical College Kolkata, and the University of Calcutta. He served as Professor of Experimental Psychology at the University of Calcutta and was president of the Indian Psychoanalytic Society.

Gisela Emma Full is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at the universities of Würzburg and Münster. In 2013, she was attested as a research fellow at European University Viadrina and the Samueli Institute.

Gisela Freund (1920–2023) was a prehistoric archaeologist. She studied at the German university of Prague (~1939–1944) and served as Head of the Department of Prehistory at Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg from ~1969 to 1987.

Gisho Nakano (1891–1977) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Junjirō Takakusu and earned a doctorate from Kyushu University. He held professorships at Peking University and Koyasan University, later serving as Koyasan's president.
Giuliana Martini is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. In 2010, she held posts at both the Italian School of East Asian Studies and Kyoto University.

Giuseppe Bardelli (1815–1865) was an Italian scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied under Giuseppe Mezzofanti, Eugène Burnouf, and Stanislas Julien. From ~1851 to 1865, he taught Coptic and Sanskrit at the University of Pisa.
Giuseppe Mezzofanti (1774–1849) studied at the University of Bologna from ~1786 to 1797. He subsequently held a post at the University of Bologna from ~1797 to 1831.

Giuseppe Tucci (1894–1984) was an Italian scholar of Tibetology, Indology, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Rome and Visva-Bharati University, later serving as professor at the University of Rome and president of the Italian Institute for the Middle and Far East.

Giuseppe Vignato specializes in history, archaeology, sinology, and Buddhist studies. He pursued doctoral studies at Peking University under teachers including Su Bai, Chongfeng Li, Shichang Ma, and Angela Falco Howard, and was attested in a post there in 2017.
